pr.title: fix(code): explain worktree collisions instead of leaking git's fatal
pr.body:
Navigation, `sync`, and `new --prepend` leaked git's raw `fatal: '<branch>' is already used by worktree at ...` followed by `git exited with status 128`. The refusal is correct; what was missing was git-stk saying what to do about it.

Now they name the destination and both ways out. Checked *before* the switch rather than after: `status` replays git's captured stderr on failure, so a post-check would have left the raw fatal on screen underneath our message. Detection is structural, never string-matching git's wording, which varies by version and locale.

<!-- git-stk:closes -->
Closes #278
<!-- /git-stk:closes -->

expected.description: The worktree-collision message tells users to free a branch with `git worktree remove`, which deletes the other worktree and any work in it, when detaching it is enough.

prior_bot.note: bot reviewed the message only for path quoting
